## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ananusociyajātaka* (Ja 328), titled *Grieve Not* in English, belongs to the fourth section (Catukkanipāta) of the Jātaka collection [Kariyawasam 2003; Fausböll 1883]. The framing narrative at Jetavana describes the Buddha delivering the discourse to console a bereaved landowner who was incapacitated with sorrow after the death of his wife [Fausböll 1883]. In the concluding identification of the birth tale (*samodhāna*), the deceased wife Sammillabhāsinī is identified with Rāhulamātā, and the ascetic sage is revealed to have been the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1883].

A remote narrative parallel has been noted in the *Mahābhārata*, which engages with the Buddhist ideal of indifference toward the death of a beloved relative [Söhnen-Thieme]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus identifies five internal Pali text-reuse matches with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (matching 826 characters, primarily covering §0.4–5.1 against §731_10–743), with no automated cross-language parallels registered at a score of 10 or higher [DharmaNexus].

- [Fausböll 1883] V. Fausböll, Jātaka Together with Its Commentary, Vol. 3 (1883) — Supplies the opening verse cue, framing story details, and the closing identification (samodhāna).
- [Kariyawasam 2003] Tilokasundari Kariyawasam, Buddhism and Psychology (2003) — Notes its placement in the Fourth Nipāta and discusses the sublimation of desire and celibacy of the couple.
